chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who completed his Hajj, then turned back, and when he exited the Sanctuary, game approached him near the Sanctuary, and the game was heading towards the Sanctuary. He threw at it and killed it. What is upon him in that regard? He said: He must ransom it.

key_terms.حَرَم: Sanctuary (specifically the sacred area of Mecca)
key_terms.يَفْدِيهِ: He must ransom it (pay compensation for the hunted animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who hunts game after exiting Ihram but while still within the Haram boundaries?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the boundary of the Haram's sanctity regarding hunting, establishing that the prohibition extends to game entering the sacred zone even after the pilgrim has technically exited Ihram. Scholars utilize this to distinguish between the ritual state of Ihram and the permanent sanctity of the Haram's airspace, emphasizing that the act of hunting within this zone remains a violation requiring fidyah. This ruling underscores the continuity of the pilgrim's restricted status concerning game until they fully depart the sacred precincts.
